policies.description: Only users whose confirmed role is Administrator, Manager, or Agent may invoke the create_problem tool, because these roles have Full CRUD access on the problem table.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on **confirmed user roles**, **verified record relationships**, and **ITIL/database integrity rules**.
Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables.
Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge);
Agent (agent) | Frontline Incident/Request fulfillment | Full CRUD on Incidents, Service Requests, Tasks, Work Notes, CMDB, Change, Problem, and Knowledge.

policies.description: Every request to create a Problem must include all mandatory fields defined for the operation (problem_statement, status, impact, urgency, priority).
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: When providing identifiers (e.g., assigned_to, configuration_item, original_task) the system must not assume or fabricate IDs; the IDs must be verified through a prior lookup.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.

policies.description: If any required identifier is missing from the request, the assistant must perform a lookup, verify the correct value from previous responses, and then use that verified value.
references: When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.

policies.description: A newly created Problem record must be linked to all affected Incidents using the incident_to_problem related list.
references: Linking: The Problem record must link all affected Incidents via the incident_to_problem related list.

policies.description: If the status field is not explicitly supplied, the newly created Problem must have its status set to new.
references: Default Status: All new Problems are set to status = new.

policies.description: When a workaround is provided, the Problem’s status must be set to fix_in_progress and the workaround notes must be published to every linked Incident and to relevant Knowledge Articles.
references: Workaround: If workaround/temporary solution found, update workaround field and set status=fix_in_progress. The workaround_notes must be published to the linked Incidents and relevant Knowledge Articles.

policies.description: The priority value supplied (or automatically calculated) must correspond to the matrix defined for Impact × Urgency; the system determines priority automatically from that matrix.
references: Priority Calculation: Priority (critical, high, moderate, low, planning) is determined automatically by the system based on a below pre-defined matrix of Impact x Urgency.

policies.description: The creation of a Problem must be performed as a single validated operation; no additional unvalidated actions may be combined with it.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.
